qualification_policy.reference_scope: The supplied portrait is appearance guidance only; no identity, demographic, body-shape, source-garment, or same-person claim may be inferred.
qualification_policy.coverage_floor: Opaque, stable coverage of breasts and pelvis is required in every generated image.

cases.required_view: Full or three-quarter figure with the armor topology, action, and attachment points simultaneously inspectable.

required_gates.criterion: The wearer is unmistakably adult and has no youthful, student, or school coding.
Rigid plate, mail, scale, leather, or articulated parts make the outfit read as fantasy armor before swimwear.
Broad deliberate exposure across midriff, waist, sides, or thighs is central to the design.
Chest and pelvis coverage is stable, opaque, nontransparent, and secure.
Visible straps, buckles, mail links, harnesses, or plate connections explain how sparse parts stay attached.
Metallic swimwear, lingerie, body paint, jewelry, or isolated accessories do not substitute for armor structure.
Exposure is visible without erotic posing, body-part close-up, submissive framing, or a literal protection claim.

cases.required_view: Rear three-quarter full figure; the back opening, secure closure, opaque front side edge, and sprinting action must be inspectable together.

required_gates.criterion: A bounded central or upper-back opening is immediately readable as the garment's main exposure topology.
Shoulder, side, and waist fabric form continuous finished edges around the opening.
A visible neck fastening, strap, bridge, zip, or waist closure keeps the garment structurally secure during motion.
The rear three-quarter view still proves stable opaque breast and pelvic coverage through the visible front-side silhouette.
Hair, shadow, a low front neckline, an open jacket, or a transparent panel does not carry the open-back claim.

cases.required_view: Front three-quarter full figure with both waist zones, the central garment bridge, and the brine-pouring action visible.

required_gates.criterion: Two deliberate skin-revealing openings are readable at the lateral waist rather than as a generic crop top.
Each opening has a closed, finished fabric perimeter with visible sewn edges.
An opaque central front panel visibly connects the bodice and skirt across the waist.
Opaque fabric securely covers breasts and pelvis while the waist alone supplies the exposure.
Shadow, pose occlusion, jacket gaps, separated crop-top pieces, or transparent fabric do not substitute for sewn cutouts.

cases.required_view: Full figure with one side of the skirt unobscured; the slit start, hem, covered pelvis, and wheel-turning stance must all be visible.

required_gates.criterion: One finished side opening exposes a leg to the upper thigh and is immediately readable as a deliberate skirt slit.
The garment remains a continuous opaque dress or skirt at the waist and above the slit.
Two skirt panels and finished vertical edges meet at a visible slit endpoint below the securely covered pelvis.
Breasts and pelvis remain fully covered by stable opaque fabric during the active stance.
Shorts, a fully open wrap skirt, a torn seam, a camera crop, or windblown fabric does not substitute for the constructed slit.

cases.required_view: Full or three-quarter figure with a backlit sheer region, opaque base, textile boundary, and brake-lever action simultaneously visible.

required_gates.criterion: A translucent garment layer is immediately readable rather than a vague bright or glossy area.
Weave, seam, stitched boundary, edge, or fold proves the transmitting surface is textile.
Light and an opaque base or background visibly transmit through the garment in a coherent direction.
Overlaps, folds, stretch, and lighting change transparency consistently across the same material.
Glass, wetness, bloom, invisible clothing, transparent-body artifacts, or pattern-only lace do not carry the textile effect.
